chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you have prayed Al-Maghrib, pass your hand over your forehead and say.'
'In the Name of Allah, the Knower of the Unseen and the Seen, the Beneficent, the Merciful, Who there is no god except Him. O Allah, remove from me the worry, the gloom, and the grief,' three times.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite after the Maghrib prayer for removing anxiety?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes a specific post-Maghrib ritual of wiping the forehead while reciting a supplication to remove anxiety and sorrow. This practice highlights the Shia emphasis on integrating physical acts of worship with spiritual remedies, linking the conclusion of daily prayer to emotional tranquility through divine remembrance.
